rationale: C20 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both letters open by transmitting draft legislation that implements a recommendation in an earlier presidential message, briefly justify the measure by reference to changed conditions including increased living costs, mention an enclosed department head's letter explaining the draft, and seek prompt congressional action. C05 and C19 share much of the same transmission-and-enclosure machinery, but lack C20's additional substantive parallel concerning adjustment in response to increased living costs.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Administrator of Veterans Affairs has prepared and submitted to me a draft of legislation which implements the recommendation in my message.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am transmitting herewith a draft of a bill... It is designed to carry out a recommendation contained in my message on February 2 to the Congress.
shared_material.explanation: Both characterize the transmitted bill as implementing a recommendation made in an earlier presidential message.

shared_material.child_excerpt: to offset rises in the cost of living since the last increase in 1957 and to adjust rates
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Since the last increase in the minimum wage both living costs and productivity have increased... the proposed bill merely reflects an adjustment to keep pace with these factors.
shared_material.explanation: Both justify a proposed rate increase as an adjustment necessitated by increased living costs since the previous increase.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am, therefore, transmitting the Administrator's letter of justification and the accompanying draft bill. I strongly recommend early enactment
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am also enclosing the letter I received from the Secretary of Labor commenting briefly upon the provisions in the draft bill... I urge its prompt consideration.
shared_material.explanation: Both close the legislative submission by identifying an enclosed agency-head explanation and urging prompt congressional action.
